crime.value: Serial murder spree — a killer has shot seven victims (including a five-year-old boy) around Edmonton; the open question is the killer's identity and how he evades a fifty-mile roadblock. The story ends with the eighth killing about to occur inside the car.
crime.quote: “So far they found seven of his victims.”

victim.value: The red-headed hitchhiking kid — a baby-faced runt who deliberately courted publicity by matching the killer's description, making himself the killer's target/rival
victim.quote: “I look just like the killer. Everybody’s scared of me. I like that.”

closed_world.value: A speeding car on an empty flat highway through wheat fields, roads blocked for fifty miles around Edmonton — no house, no tree, only one isolated gas station
closed_world.quote: The road stretched ahead of us and on both sides there was nothing but the flat plain. Not a house. Not a tree.

culprit_and_motive.value: The narrator/driver is the actual serial killer, hair dyed brown; he hunted the highway for the copycat attention-seeker, killing out of compulsion and to eliminate the imposter stealing his notoriety

resolution.value: No restoration of order — reversal reveal: the reader realizes the driver is the killer and the kid becomes victim number eight
resolution.quote: He was going to be number eight.

investigator.value: First-person narrator-driver, apparently a neutral motorist, in fact the culprit — an unreliable lens whose calm questioning mimics interrogation
investigator.quote: “I know,” I said. “And I think you’ll get more. I thought I’d find you somewhere on this highway.”

suspect_architecture.value: Effectively two figures in a closed car: the red-headed hitchhiker who matches the killer's description and boasts of killing, and the unremarkable brown-haired driver. The kid is built up as the obvious suspect (appearance, manner, obsession with the murders) while the driver is differentiated only by hair color — which turns out to be dyed.

red_herring.value: The red-headed kid himself is the planted false trail — his wild talk, his gun fantasies, and his matching description direct suspicion entirely onto him, including from real police who have stopped him three times.
red_herring.quote: "I been picked up by the cops three times on this road in the last two days."

clue_fairness.value: The reader is given every clue the kid has: the narrator's nervous tightness, refusal to phone, avoiding the gas station's radio and phone, his flat 'No' about wondering why the killer did it, and his knowledge of the description. Hair color is the only stated mismatch, and dye is available as an inference.
clue_fairness.quote: "You nervous about something?" My eyes flicked in his direction. "No. Why should I be?"

social_world.value: A rural highway world of wheat fields, isolated gas stations and roadblocks, where status is measured by fear and notoriety — the kid's talk of being 'pushed' by everyone and becoming 'the tallest man in the world' with a gun frames a hierarchy of the small being dominated.
social_world.quote: "It's good to have people afraid of you... You're not short anymore when you got a gun."

alibi.value: No formal alibi; the narrator's cover is his ordinariness and the roadblocks he passes freely, plus dyed hair standing in for a disguise rather than an account of whereabouts.
alibi.quote: "The police got all the roads blocked for fifty miles around Edmonton."

reveal_mechanic.value: A single spoken line demonstrating disguise: the kid excludes the driver because of brown hair, and the driver answers that hair can be dyed — retroactively converting every earlier evasion into proof, closed by the count reaching eight.
reveal_mechanic.quote: I smiled. "But I could have dyed it."

media_and_audience.value: Radio news bulletins drive the whole story — the victim count and the killer's description are public property, and both killer and imitator measure themselves by publicity; the kid craves the same coverage as the murderer.
media_and_audience.quote: "I get as much publicity as the killer."

investigator_wound.value: Inverted: the 'investigator' figure is the killer, and the kid's amateur probing exploits his own vanity and compulsion — he is drawn to be recognized and cannot let a poser claim his notoriety.
investigator_wound.quote: "I thought I'd find you somewhere on this highway."

victims_enemies.value: No web of grievance exists — the victims are strangers chosen at random by a spree killer; the hitchhiker's only 'offense' is resembling the killer and courting the notoriety.
victims_enemies.quote: So far they found seven of his victims.

suspect_wounds.value: The red-headed kid's wound is his smallness and lifelong sense of being pushed around; he compensates by claiming the killer's glamour, which makes him look guilty to everyone including the police.
suspect_wounds.quote: “It's good to have people afraid of you,” he said. “You're not short anymore when you got a gun.”

unreliable_frame.value: The first-person driver-narrator withholds his own identity as the killer, answering questions flatly and truthfully while concealing everything; the kid in turn lies by implication about being the murderer.

setting_as_constraint.value: An empty flat prairie highway through wheat fields — no houses, no trees, gas stations forty miles apart and radioless — isolates victim and killer, while roadblocks for fifty miles around Edmonton force the killer to hide in plain sight as an ordinary motorist.
setting_as_constraint.quote: The road stretched ahead of us and on both sides there was nothing but the flat plain. Not a house. Not a tree.

evidence_type.value: Testimonial/physical self-disclosure: the broadcast description (red hair) plus the narrator's admission that hair can be dyed — the identifying physical trait is the clue.
evidence_type.quote: “No. You got brown hair. His is red. Like mine.”

false_suspect.value: The red-headed hitchhiker, picked up by police three times in two days because he fits the broadcast description perfectly and enjoys the fear it produces.
false_suspect.quote: “I been picked up by the cops three times on this road in the last two days.”

technical_detail.value: Hair dye as disguise — the manhunt keys entirely on red hair, so altering hair colour defeats the description and lets the killer drive through roadblocks.
technical_detail.quote: I smiled. “But I could have dyed it.”

moral_ambiguity.value: The kid's theory — voiced sympathetically — that a man pushed and ordered around all his life finally exploded; the killer neither confirms nor denies it, and shows a flicker of conscience about the five-year-old victim while the boastful kid does not.
moral_ambiguity.quote: “Maybe he got pushed too far. All his life somebody always pushed him.”
